hook: SCP-2700 opens like a routine hardware report: a console, a particle accelerator squeezed into a chamber far too small for it, and a glowing core nobody can explain, all credited to Nikola Tesla. Take the equipment section slowly, but know that the real weight of the article sits in a long first-person journal further down. Tesla's voice there is far from the gentle-genius image, and he airs some openly contemptuous views of humanity.
whyItMatters: It borrows a real historical figure and his unfinished Teleforce project and builds a threat on a cosmic scale on top of them. The tags place it among end-of-the-world scenarios driven by entropy and time, yet it carries that scale through one man's private writing rather than a field report. The contrast between the clinical Foundation sections and the confessional log is what tends to stay with readers.
thingsToNotice: Notice the shift in register between the cold equipment inventory and the emotional, sometimes bitter prose of the journal. Inside the journal, watch what Tesla tells his hosts versus what he admits on the page; the gap between the two is the character study. The physics is kept deliberately simple, a single reversal idea carrying the whole danger, so the drama can stay human. The final paragraphs reward a slow reread, because they answer questions the opening report never thinks to ask.
